envelope.text: ADOPT-BOUNDED as before: the period is truncated to whole milliseconds,

rename.resolution:
Executed 2026-09-05 (phase-425 W1), as ONE four-name decision plus the macro, on an owner's yes. Sweep, as the recommendation required, because half the sites are outside this report's TU set:

    rg -w create_timer packages/api/nros-cpp/ examples/ docs/ cmake/

`create_timer_oneshot`, `create_timer_in_group`, `ComponentNode::create_timer_in` and `bind_timer` KEEP the `timer` stem — recorded so the stem split is a decision, not an oversight. No deprecated alias: it would have kept the ours-only half of this pair alive permanently.

The soft collision the blocker predicted is real and harmless as predicted: `rclcpp::Node::create_wall_timer` (then `rclcpp_compat.hpp:406`; `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp:785` since phase-417 stage 6 step A deleted the shim) is a different class in a different namespace — at the time driven by its own `pump()`, and since phase-417 dispatched by the nros executor like everything else, which changes nothing here. No ODR break, no overload set.

why:
EXECUTED 2026-09-05 (phase-425 W1). `nros::Node::create_timer` -> `create_wall_timer`, with no deprecated alias, alongside the other three spellings the recommendation named (`nros::create_wall_timer` in the since-DELETED `std_compat.hpp`, both `ComponentNode` overloads, and the macro, now `NROS_CREATE_WALL_TIMER`). The name is accurate: ours is monotonic, by the RFC-0073 platform-clock contract, so it is a WALL timer in rclcpp's sense.

What is left is not a name difference and needs no campaign row of its own — the report now matches this item under the systematic `no-shared-ptr` rule (ours `(Timer&, uint64_t, cpp_timer_callback_t, void*)`, theirs `(chrono::duration, CallbackT, CallbackGroup::SharedPtr)`): caller-owned storage because there is no allocator, `uint64_t period_ms` because a freestanding build has no `<chrono>` (the chrono spelling is the free `nros::create_wall_timer` under `NROS_CPP_STD`), and a group passed to a separate `create_timer_in_group` rather than as a trailing argument.

The name this FREES is the point of the phase: rclcpp's bare `create_timer` is the CLOCK-TAKING form, and `cpp:create_timer` now records it as the gap phase-425 W4 fills.

phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding, RANKED-9, and phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) CLOSED it: the `rclcpp::Node` adapter's `create_wall_timer` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp:785`) passes `node_.create_wall_timer`'s `Result` to `detail::require_created` (`:384`), which aborts naming the verb (`abort_failed_create`, `:376`, `NROS_RCLCPP_ABORT_FAILED_CREATE`) — and this is the site where a null or dead return would have been silent above all, because a ported node stores the timer handle and never dereferences it, so a dead timer would simply never fire. The entity name passed to the diagnostic is empty: a timer has none. History, one sentence: until Q1 this site (then `:707`) was one of seven that discarded the create `Result` with an explicit `(void)` and returned a non-null `shared_ptr` to an entity that was never initialised, SILENTLY WRONG. Separately, what it returns is `std::shared_ptr<rclcpp::TimerBase>`, and our `rclcpp::TimerBase` carries none of upstream's methods; see `cpp:Timer::cancel`.

The disposition for the create-`Result` finding is recorded on `cpp:Node::create_publisher`, which carries the full statement.

phase-442 W2 (2026-09-11) — `std_compat.hpp` is DELETED, so any sentence above naming that header describes a spelling that no longer exists. It was a third orphaned vocabulary: free functions shadowing the `Node` methods a ported file calls, dead in every shipping configuration, and RFC-0096 removed the layer it belonged to. The always-available spelling is the method.

phase-476 W2 (2026-10-05) — the value-returning `create_wall_timer(period, callback)` returns a two-word `nros::TimerHandle` (`rclcpp::Timer::SharedPtr`), not a `std::shared_ptr<nros::Timer>` aliased onto a heap cell. Its callable is copied into the executor arena, which destroys it when the timer is released. It is FREESTANDING: the primary overload takes `nros::Duration`, and the `std::chrono` overload is conversion sugar over it.

issue 1974 (2026-10-20) — the value-returning overload now takes Jazzy's trailing `(group = nullptr, autostart = true)`, so under Jazzy its shape CORRESPONDS and a ported line compiles; DISPOSITION added. THE ENVELOPE is on the declaration in `node.hpp`: the period is truncated to whole milliseconds, `group` is a `const rclcpp::CallbackGroup*` (our group is a value token; a ported `nullptr` binds), and `autostart = false` creates the timer cancelled until `reset()`, as upstream. A callback invocable as `void(const rclcpp::TimerInfo&)` receives the call info (`cpp:TimerInfoCallbackType`).
